newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ALOMAR TAKES HIS TURN IN HOME RUN BINGE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ALOMAR TAKES HIS TURN IN HOME RUN BINGE.

text.p: Roberto Alomar continued baseball's home run explosion of the last two days by going deep three times Saturday and driving in six runs to power the Orioles to a 14-5 win over the Boston Red Sox.

Alomar broke out of a prolonged slump by hitting a two-run homer in the second inning off Aaron Sele (3-1), a solo blast in the fourth off Pat Mahomes and a two-run homer in the fifth off Rick Trlicek. He drove in another run with a sacrifice fly in the eighth.
They were the first three homers of the season for Alomar, who entered the game with a .205 batting average and no extra-base hits this season.

"This is the first time I had a good game this season and I feel really good about it," said Alomar, who has been bothered all season by an ankle injury. "My leg's feeling better every day that I play."
Alomar became the third player in the last two days to hit three homers. Ken Griffey of Seattle and Matt Williams of Cleveland accomplished the feat on Friday night.
Jimmy Key (4-0) remained unbeaten despite allowing five runs and eight hits in six innings, including a two-run homer by Mo Vaughn and a solo shot by Mike Stanley in the first.
In New York, Cecil Fielder ended his season-long power drought by belting a three-run homer to cap a 5-for-5 day at the plate as the Yankees clobbered the Chicago White Sox 10-2.
Fielder lined a pitch from reliever Carlos Castillo down the line in left for his first homer of the season and first in 98 at-bats since the end of the 1996 campaign.

"It's a relief that I've got somewhat of a stroke going. The home runs are going to come," the slugger said. "If you're confident and you know the game, you realise that these things (slumps) are going to happen. You have to work through it."
David Cone (2-2) went seven innings for the win.
In Toronto, Joe Carter singled home Otis Nixon for the winning run in the ninth inning as the Toronto Blue Jays snapped the Seattle Mariners' five-game road winning streak with a 4-3 victory.
Paul Quantrill (3-1) allowed three hits in two scoreless innings for the win, extending his string of scoreless innings to 10 2/3.

In Oakland, Mitch "Wild Thing" Williams struck again, uncorking a wild pitch with the bases loaded in the bottom of the 11th that allowed the Oakland Athletics to complete a four-run rally and post a 7-6 win over the Kansas City Royals.

After the Royals scored three times in the top of the 11th, Scott Spiezio led off the bottom half with a single off Jason Jacome. One out later, Jason Giambi belted a two-run homer and Matt Stairs followed with his third of the year and second extra-inning blast in three days to even the score.
Williams (0-1) came on and retired the first batter before Damon Mashore walked, stole second and went to third on Rafael Bournigal's infield single.

Mark McGwire was intentionally walked for the third time to load the bases and Williams fired a high fastball to Jose Canseco on an 0-2 count. The ball deflected off catcher Mike Sweeney's glove, allowing Mashore to score the winning run.
Aaron Small (3-0) earned the win, despite surrendering three runs in the top of the 11th.
In Anaheim, Brian Moehler threw a two-hitter for his first career complete game and shutout and Damion Easley and Travis Fryman hit solo homers as the Detroit Tigers blanked the Anaheim Angels 2-0.
Moehler (2-1), making just his seventh career start, retired the final 16 batters and he struck out four without walking a single batter in the shutout.
Hard-luck loser Chuck Finley (0-1) allowed just five hits in eight innings.

In Milwaukee, Jeff Huson's RBI single down the left-field line in the bottom of the ninth capped a three-run rally against closer Jose Mesa as the Brewers snapped a six-game losing streak with a 9-8 victory over the Cleveland Indians.
Jeromy Burnitz knotted the game 8-8 with a two-run double to right and then scored on Huson's hit.
Doug Jones (1-0) notched the victory.
Matt Williams hit two more homers for Cleveland and has five in the last two games.
At Minnesota, Bobby Witt continued his mastery of Minnesota with 6 1/3 strong innings as the Texas Rangers won their fourth game in a row, 6-1 over the Twins.
Witt, who has a personal six-game winning streak against the Twins and is now 17-5 lifetime against them, allowed seven hits to improve to 4-0 for the first time in his career.
Dean Palmer and Damon Buford each had three hits to pace the Rangers' 11-hit attack.
